question.worked_solution:
First we apply the quotient rule, subtracting exponents in the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{n}{{n}^{4}}\cdot {n}^{8} & = \\ {n}^{1-4}\cdot {n}^{8} & = \\ {n}^{-3}\cdot {n}^{8} & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then we apply the product rule, adding exponents in the product:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{n}^{-3}\cdot {n}^{8} & = \\ {n}^{-3+8} & = \\ {n}^{5} & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{n}{{n}^{4}}\cdot {n}^{8}={n}^{5}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
